method: Every selected pinned Hebrew verse and annotation read before drafting; individual English lines and rationales composed from the Hebrew. All 714 TSW comparator verses read afterward. No synonym replacement engine or overlap quota.

focused_reread.qualification: Reread by the drafting agent, not independent scholarly review.

post_reread_adjustments.decision: Removed an unnecessary becoming-fools interpretation; retained fools as the subject of suffering for their wrongdoing.
Removed unsupported all before my glory while retaining the difficult glory expression and explanatory note.
Removed the supplied field; corpses fill the judged nations in the selected reading.
Shortened the exhaustion clause while retaining whole-being longing for salvation.
Unpacked name as what it proclaims to make the difficult utterance-above-name clause readable; the note records the literal expression and alternatives.
Matched the established YAH typography and checked full LORD and short YAH separately against every selected source verse.

priority_findings: All 717 original records bind exactly once to 714 public verses. Separate titles in Psalms 108, 140, and 142 join public verse 1.
Psalms 105–106 retain divine hardening, the negative in 105:28, falling in 106:27, and the cost of violence including child sacrifice.
Psalm 107 retains sea in the directional list, distinct rescue verbs, four identical thanksgiving refrains, and all source scribal notes in the ledger.
Psalm 109 retains the singular target and the uncertainty whether the curse passage is petition or quoted hostile speech; family harm is explicit.
Psalm 110 preserves LORD/lord/Adonai distinctions and flags difficult youth/dew and priesthood expressions.
Psalms 111–112 preserve twenty-two poetic units; Psalm 119 preserves all 176 verses and twenty-two eight-verse stanzas with consistent instruction vocabulary.
All fifteen Songs of Ascents retain titles and their compact poetic structure; slavery, gendered family images, and disturbing petitions are not generalized away.
Psalm 136 retains its complete refrain in all twenty-six verses, including the violent historical clauses.
Psalm 137 retains the final retaliatory wish against little children as the exiles’ speech.
Psalm 139:16 explicitly follows the written negative and documents the divergent read form; Psalms 140–141 retain difficult clauses and source variants in the apparatus.
Psalm 144 retains my people, two divine hands, ten strings, sons and daughters, and thousands/tens of thousands.
companion_impact: Psalms 105–144 quotations and bindings need later reconciliation; Companion was not modified.
continuation_authorization: Successive forty-chapter blocks authorized without routine approval pauses; source and QA standards unchanged.
